questions.q: According to this lesson, which testnet is Ethereum's current recommended testnet for application and smart contract testing?
options: Goerli
Holesky
Sepolia
Hoodi
questions.explain: Goerli was deprecated in 2024; Sepolia is the current recommended testnet for application/contract testing, while Hoodi (which replaced the now-defunct Holesky) focuses on staking and protocol-level testing.

questions.q: What does a clean, successful testnet deployment genuinely prove about a contract?
options: That it's safe from all economic attacks
That the deployment script's mechanics work — constructor arguments, ordering, bytecode size, and basic integrations
That it will behave identically under real mainnet gas congestion
That it has no exploitable bugs of any kind
questions.explain: A testnet deployment validates the mechanical side — the script, the bytecode, basic integrations — not the contract's economic safety under real conditions.

questions.q: Why does testnet ETH having zero value limit what a testnet deployment can prove?
options: It doesn't limit anything — testnets are identical to mainnet in every way
Because there's no real economic incentive for an attacker to exploit a testnet deployment, so testnets see none of the adversarial pressure a funded mainnet contract faces
Because testnet transactions can't be verified
Because testnets don't support Solidity
questions.explain: Zero-value testnet ETH means no one has a real incentive to attack a testnet deployment, so adversarial behavior mainnet contracts actually face goes untested.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT something a testnet deployment can be relied on to validate, per this lesson?
options: Whether the deploy script's constructor arguments are correct
Whether the contract's bytecode fits under the size limit
Whether the contract is safe under real mainnet liquidity depth and MEV pressure
Whether basic integration with testnet infrastructure behaves as expected
questions.explain: Real liquidity depth and MEV pressure don't exist on a testnet — those are exactly the economic conditions a testnet deployment can't validate.

questions.q: What is the "right mental model" for testnet success, according to this lesson?
options: Testnet success means mainnet is guaranteed to be safe
Testnet success proves the mechanics work, not that the economics are safe — later lessons (pre-launch checklist, phased rollouts) exist because of that gap
Testnet deployments are pointless and should be skipped
Testnet and mainnet are functionally identical environments
questions.explain: The lesson's core framing: a testnet proves the deployment mechanics, not economic safety — which is exactly why Chapter 3 later adds phased rollouts and value caps.
